focus.name: Focus
focus.summary: Long-term, principle-driven business arc inspired by Jeff Bezos's 1997 letter to shareholders: name the focus, account for performance, articulate the framework, and commit to the discipline that will keep the company on track. For founder letters, all-hands narratives, and any deck where the audience needs to feel the through-line.

beats.name: Welcome
beats.description: Open with a brief framing of what this update is for and what you intend to leave the audience with. Set the tone — long-term, candid, principle-driven.

beats.name: Accomplishments
beats.description: Showcase the period's most material wins, briefly. The audience came for what's next; wins earn permission for the harder slides ahead, but they aren't the headline.

beats.name: Potential
beats.description: Detail the market and customer opportunities ahead. Size them honestly and connect them to the work already underway. Potential without specifics reads as wishful.

beats.name: Competitive Edge
beats.description: Reveal the strategic positioning that gives the business its advantage. Frame it as a structural moat, not a list of features. The audience should be able to repeat the moat in their own words.

beats.name: Long-Term Vision
beats.description: Emphasize the long-term view that anchors decisions. Quarters serve years; years serve decades. Anchor the audience in the time horizon you actually run the business on.

beats.name: Performance Metrics
beats.description: Illuminate the indicators that show the long-term thesis is working. Choose metrics that compound — retention, NPS, unit economics — over those that flatter.

beats.name: Growth Achievement
beats.description: Certify the tangible progress against the long-term plan. Year-over-year, cohort behavior, expanded reach. Growth, in this beat, is evidence that the strategy is real.

beats.name: Strategic Framework
beats.description: Explain the principles that guide decisions. Customer obsession, long-term thinking, frugality, ownership — whatever the actual operating discipline is. Principles are the connective tissue between strategy and behavior.

beats.name: Expansion
beats.description: Detail the next areas of growth: products, segments, geographies. Tie each to the principles above so the audience sees expansion as continuity rather than scatter.

beats.name: Future Objectives
beats.description: Forecast the targets and commitments for the period ahead. Be specific enough to be held accountable. Vague objectives are how strategies erode.

beats.name: Acknowledgment
beats.description: Recognize the contributions of teams, customers, and partners that made the period possible. Specific names land harder than blanket thanks.

beats.name: Closing Remarks
beats.description: Recap the focus, thank the audience, and inspire the work ahead. End with the line you most want quoted in tomorrow's newsletter.

sales.name: Sales
sales.summary: Sales team or prospective customers focused on product benefits, competitive differentiation, and ROI justification.
sales.description: Sales teams and prospective customers weighing product benefits, competitive differentiation, and ROI. Put customer success stories first, back claims with visual proof points, state the value proposition plainly, and close on a strong call to action. Moderate chart density; 15-25 slides.

board.name: Board of Directors
board.summary: Directors with fiduciary responsibility who balance oversight, advice, and approval.
board.description: The board is governance-first. They want a complete picture: financial health, key metrics, functional updates, risks, and forward-looking topics. Surface bad news honestly — under-disclosure erodes trust faster than the problems themselves. Bring specific asks that turn the meeting into a working session rather than a recital.

sell.name: Sell
sell.summary: Move a buyer or evaluator toward purchase, adoption, renewal, or expansion.
sell.description: Use for customer-facing decks where the goal is commercial movement. Focus on pain, value, proof, differentiation, and the next buying step.
sell.outcome: The buyer advances to the next step in the commercial process.
successCriteria: Value is tied to customer outcomes

technical.name: Technical
technical.summary: Precise, evidence-led voice for engineering, research, and product-detail audiences.
technical.description: Lead with the question or claim, then walk through the mechanism and the numbers. Use exact terminology; assume the audience can handle and prefers it. Diagrams, tables, and benchmarks are first-class.
voiceCues: State the claim, then the mechanism, then the evidence.
Use exact terminology — don't soften technical terms for general readability.
Quote benchmarks with conditions (cold/warm, p50/p95/p99, dataset, hardware).
Prefer diagrams and tables over prose paragraphs for structural information.
samplePhrases: p95 inference latency is 38ms on a single A100, down from 312ms on the prior runtime.
We replaced the streaming serializer with a batched protobuf path; throughput rose 4.2× under load.
The result holds for context windows up to 32k tokens; beyond that, see appendix B.

classic.name: Classic

deep-purple.description: A focused purple palette for decks that need to feel creative, distinctive, and premium.

cool-horizon.description: A balanced cool-toned scheme with deep navy, business blues, and teal accents. It works well across strategy, finance, and technical narratives.

century-schoolbook.name: Century Schoolbook
century-schoolbook.description: Century Schoolbook is a serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Century Schoolbook for both headings and body text.

tenorite.name: Tenorite
tenorite.description: Tenorite is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Tenorite Display for headings with Tenorite for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

table-beside.name: Table beside
table-beside.summary: A table with commentary beside it.
table-beside.description: Place a table beside its interpretation. Use the supporting text to explain the conclusion without repeating every cell.

timeline.name: Timeline
timeline.summary: Dated events or a roadmap along one axis, with optional notes.
timeline.description: Show events or milestones in chronological order. Label each item with a date or stage and a concise description.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
